_comment: THE PANEL'S RAIL, as a stage. Same schema and same renderer as stage.json - the
console's room - so there is one way to describe a picture in this project and not two.
WHY IT IS A STAGE NOW. The rail used to be ONE sprite: a single .rkspr drawn straight
into an <Image>. That made the character her own background, which has two costs.
(1) Whatever is behind her has to be baked into her, so she cannot be moved or swapped
without a hole appearing where she used to be. (2) Every new pose has to redraw the
backdrop too. Splitting them means the bed is drawn once, she sits on top of it, and
moving her is a change to 'at' - nothing else. [R-064]
WHAT CARRIES THE STATE. Her eyes cannot: at 120x200 her iris is two or three pixels
and the 24-colour reduction does not even keep a green for it (measured). So the
NEON SIGN over the bed is the readout - 1,245 pixels of it - and the pose timings that
used to live in panel-model.ps1 as KeeperLoops now live here as 'hold':
run    slow pulse   - a light breathing every few seconds reads as 'fine'
care   even pulse   - something is waiting
halt   fast blink   - a fault indicator, which is this pose's whole job
sleep  held, lit    - nothing is running, so nothing MOVES
SLEEP USED TO HOLD THE DIM FRAME ('nothing is running, so nothing is lit') and that was
the thing Eva actually complained about: the sign looked like the colour had drained out of
the picture rather than like a state. It is also unreadable now that the sign carries words -
at 43% alpha the text sits at 1.69:1 against its own slab, so the one sentence in the room
faded out in the exact state it names. Held and LIT: 5.04:1, and 'held' still separates it
from run's slow pulse and halt's 1:1 blink, which is what carried the meaning anyway.
She is one static frame. That is honest rather than lazy: there is only one drawing of
her in this pose, and a second frame that changed nothing would be a lie about it.
Adding a pose means dropping a file in art\ and naming it here.
Built by build-belka.ps1, which remembers the substitutions (X -> * is the sign,
T -> + its halo). Re-importing loses them; re-running that script puts them back.

layers._note: the bed, from above, nobody on it. The sign over the headboard is the status light.

her, lying on it. 260x434 centred in 296x600. The rail is the same 320px wide on screen as before - what changed is that this stage draws at 1x instead of 2x, so the same strip holds four times the pixels. Measured reason: at 130x217 both irises together were ELEVEN pixels. Her iris is the state colour here too, mapped by rectangle - and note it is NOT green any more: median cut allocates by area, forty pixels of iris lose, and the entry they land in is a blue-grey the hair also uses. The rectangle is what makes marking it safe.
